card.name: Words leading into prices and costs
card.fires_on: Words in economics or finance text that come just before a price, rate or cost is stated, such as "at" after "sold oil" or "above-market" rates.

modes.label: Selling or buying at a price
modes.description: The word "at" or "low" after a verb of selling or buying, where a price level comes next.
modes.example: Soviet aid was particularly important because the Soviet Union sold North Korea oil<< at>> low prices.

modes.label: Accounting steps
modes.description: Words in a list of cash-flow steps, such as non-cash items and depreciation.
modes.example: Start with net income. Add back non-cash<< expenses>>. (Such as depreciation and amortization

modes.label: Market-rate wording
modes.description: Hyphenated or linking words describing rates relative to the market.
modes.example: to pay for the above<<-market>> rates that solar power producers get.
